How Much Does Contract Staffing Cost in Tamil Nadu? (2026)

தமிழ்நாட்டில் ஒப்பந்த பணியாளர் செலவு

A contract worker in Tamil Nadu costs the gross wage plus statutory dues (employer PF 12%, ESI 3.25% for wages up to Rs 21,000, bonus of at least 8.33%, gratuity of about 4.81%), plus the agency service charge, plus 18% GST. In the worked example below, statutory dues add about 15 to 16% to an Rs 18,000 gross wage. Lifeline Placements quotes on WhatsApp: +91 99622 99076.

How much does a contract worker cost in Tamil Nadu?

Total monthly cost = gross wage + employer statutory dues + agency service charge, plus 18% GST. Statutory dues for a worker earning Rs 18,000 gross come to about Rs 2,770 to Rs 2,940 a month in our example, roughly 15 to 16% of gross. The service charge depends on role, volume and duration.

What goes into the cost?

ComponentRate (as of Nov 2026)Applied to
Employer PF (EPF + EPS)12%PF wages (basic + DA). Mandatory up to the wage ceiling: Rs 15,000, reported raised to Rs 25,000 from 17 Sep 2026. Confirm with EPFO.
EDLI0.5%PF wages
PF admin charges0.5%PF wages
Employer ESI3.25%Gross wages, for employees earning up to Rs 21,000 a month
Bonus (minimum)8.33%Bonus wages, capped at Rs 7,000 or the applicable minimum wage, whichever is higher
Gratuity provisionabout 4.81%Basic + DA (15 days' wages per year of service ÷ 26 working days)
Agency service chargequoted in writing for each requirement before you commitAs agreed
GST18%Generally the full invoice value for manpower supply. Confirm with your GST adviser.

Worked example: Rs 18,000 gross a month

Assume gross wage Rs 18,000, with basic + DA of Rs 9,000 (the Code on Wages requires excluded allowances to stay within 50% of total pay, so wages must be at least half of gross).

ItemCalculationRs per month
Gross wageGiven18,000
Employer PF12% × 9,0001,080
EDLI + PF admin1% × 9,00090
Employer ESI3.25% × 18,000585
Bonus8.33% × 7,000 to 9,000 (depends on the applicable minimum wage)583 to 750
Gratuity provision4.81% × 9,000433
Cost before service charge and GST20,771 to 20,938

Add the agency service charge, then GST at 18%. Leave wages, uniforms, transport, canteen and overtime are extra where they apply. This example is illustrative. Your figures depend on the wage structure and the minimum wage for your scheduled employment and zone.

What is the minimum wage in Tamil Nadu?

Tamil Nadu sets minimum wages per scheduled employment and zone, revised twice a year through the variable dearness allowance. The latest revision applies from 1 April 2026 (notification dated 18 February 2026). For shops and commercial establishments the reported VDA is Rs 7,353 a month, added to the basic rate for your category.

Check the exact rate for your employment and zone on the Tamil Nadu Labour Department website before fixing wages.

How much does a manpower agency charge in Chennai?

For permanent placement, published market rates run from about 8.33% to 16.67% of the hire's annual CTC. For contract staffing, agencies add a monthly service charge to wages and statutory dues, plus 18% GST. Rates depend on role, volume and duration. Related questions

How much does a manpower agency charge in Chennai?

For permanent placement, published market rates run from about 8.33% to 16.67% of the hire's annual CTC. For contract staffing, agencies add a monthly service charge on top of wages and statutory dues, plus 18% GST. Rates depend on role, volume and duration. Lifeline Placements' fee: quoted in writing for each requirement before you commit. Send your role on WhatsApp for a written quote.

Is GST charged on the full invoice or only the service charge?

For manpower supply, GST at 18% is generally charged on the full value billed, including the wages reimbursed, not only on the agency's service charge. Most registered businesses can claim input tax credit on it. Confirm the treatment for your business with your GST adviser before you compare quotes.

Do contract workers get PF and ESI?

Yes. PF and ESI apply to contract workers just as to direct employees, subject to the wage limits. The agency, as the employer, deducts the employee share, adds the employer share and deposits both. As principal employer, you should check monthly challans, because unpaid dues can become your liability.
